# Answer formats

<!-- Generated by `bun scripts/answer-formats.ts` from packages/schemas. Do not edit by hand: a test compares
     this file with the generated output. -->

Every answer a paste-it-yourself run can ask for. Each prompt ends with the exact JSON Schema its answer is
checked against; this page is the same thing made readable — every field, what goes in it, whether it can be
left out, and an example value. The job page shows the same interface for the question in front of you. How the
whole flow works is in [WITHOUT_API_KEYS](WITHOUT_API_KEYS.md).

Examples describe one small story — *The Lamp at Vell*: Ines, a lighthouse engineer; Tomas, the old keeper; the
lighthouse itself; Ines's weather notebook. Each complete example below is a valid answer, checked by the tests.

## StoryAnalysis

Asked by **Analyse story** — reads the story and proposes the cast, places, props and chapters.

```ts
/** The story bible read from the source text: cast, places, props, world and chapter breakdown. */
interface StoryAnalysis {
  /**
   * The story's title.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "The Lamp at Vell"
   */
  title?: string;
  /**
   * A short summary of the whole story. Shown for review with the analysis.
   * @example "A lighthouse engineer sent to shut down the old light at Vell finds its keeper will not leave, and a storm forces them to keep the lamp burning together."
   */
  summary: string;
  /**
   * The main genre. Shown for review with the analysis.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "drama"
   */
  genre?: string;
  /**
   * A narrower genre within it. Shown for review with the analysis.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "maritime slice of life"
   */
  subgenre?: string;
  /**
   * The story's overall tone. Shown for review with the analysis.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "quiet, bittersweet, hopeful"
   */
  tone?: string;
  /**
   * What the story is about underneath the plot, one per item.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   * @example ["duty","letting go","old and new ways"]
   */
  themes?: string[];
  /**
   * Where the story takes place. Goes into the project's world notes (if it has none yet), which planning receives.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "a remote lighthouse on a rocky northern coast"
   */
  setting?: string;
  /**
   * When the story takes place; added next to the setting in the world notes.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "late 1950s"
   */
  period?: string;
  /**
   * How fast the story moves. Shown for review with the analysis.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "slow build to a storm-night climax"
   */
  pacing?: string;
  /**
   * Images that recur through the story, one per item. Added to the project's world notes.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   * @example ["the turning beam","rain on glass","the open notebook"]
   */
  visualMotifs?: string[];
  /**
   * The key of the main character. Must equal one of `characters[].key`.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "ines"
   */
  protagonistKey?: string;
  /**
   * Everyone who appears or acts in the story, once each. Each becomes a character in the project's cast, unless one with the same key or name already exists.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   */
  characters?: {
    /**
     * A short lowercase slug for this character. Other fields refer to the character by this key.
     * At least 1 characters.
     * @example "ines"
     */
    key: string;
    /**
     * The character's name as it appears in the cast list.
     * At least 1 characters.
     * @example "Ines Varga"
     */
    name: string;
    /**
     * Other names, epithets or descriptions the text uses for the same person, so they are not counted twice.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["the engineer","Miss Varga"]
     */
    aliases?: string[];
    /**
     * The character's part in the story.
     * Optional — defaults to "supporting" when left out.
     * @example "protagonist"
     */
    role: "protagonist" | "antagonist" | "supporting" | "minor";
    /**
     * What the character looks like and how they behave, precise enough to draw them the same in every panel. It becomes the character's first design version.
     */
    bible: {
      /**
       * How the character presents, as it should be drawn.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "woman"
       */
      genderPresentation?: string;
      /**
       * Apparent age, best as a number range.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "early 30s"
       */
      ageRange?: string;
      /**
       * Height, ideally relative to the rest of the cast.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "tall, a head above Tomas"
       */
      height?: string;
      /**
       * Body shape and frame.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "lean, long-limbed"
       */
      build?: string;
      /**
       * The shape of the face.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "narrow oval with a pointed chin"
       */
      faceShape?: string;
      /**
       * Skin tone. The image prompt adds the word "skin" after it.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "light olive"
       */
      skinTone?: string;
      /**
       * Eye shape and colour.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "hooded grey eyes"
       */
      eyes?: string;
      /**
       * Eyebrow shape and colour.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "straight dark brows"
       */
      eyebrows?: string;
      /**
       * Nose shape.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "long straight nose"
       */
      nose?: string;
      /**
       * Mouth and lips.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "thin lips, often pressed together"
       */
      mouth?: string;
      /**
       * Exact hair colour, length and style.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "shoulder-length black hair tied back, a silver streak at the left temple"
       */
      hair?: string;
      /**
       * Beard or moustache; leave empty when there is none.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example ""
       */
      facialHair?: string;
      /**
       * Visible marks that help tell the character apart, one per item.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example ["small faded mark on the right cheekbone","ink stains on the fingertips"]
       */
      distinctiveFeatures?: string[];
      /**
       * The default outfit with colours and materials. It becomes the character's "Default" outfit and is drawn whenever a panel names no other outfit.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "navy oilskin coat over a grey wool jumper, dark canvas trousers, black rubber boots"
       */
      wardrobe?: string;
      /**
       * Things the character wears besides clothes, one per item.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example ["round wire glasses","brass pocket watch"]
       */
      accessories?: string[];
      /**
       * Weapons the character carries, one per item; empty when none.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example []
       */
      weapons?: string[];
      /**
       * Objects the character usually carries, one per item.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example ["weather notebook","pencil stub"]
       */
      props?: string[];
      /**
       * Personality in a few words. Kept apart from appearance so it never reaches the drawing as a look.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "precise, stubborn, quietly kind"
       */
      personality?: string;
      /**
       * How the personality shows in posture and gesture; the image prompt uses it for the character's reference sheet.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "taps her pencil against the notebook when thinking"
       */
      visualMannerisms?: string;
      /**
       * The expression the character wears when a panel does not say otherwise.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "focused, slight frown"
       */
      defaultExpression?: string;
      /**
       * 3-6 short, visible identity markers that must stay the same in every panel. The image prompt lists them as "never change". Never put personality or plot facts here.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example ["silver streak in black hair","round wire glasses","navy oilskin coat"]
       */
      immutableTraits?: string[];
      /**
       * Other outfits the character wears in the story. Each one with a description becomes an extra outfit for the character, next to the default wardrobe.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       */
      outfitVariants?: {
        /**
         * A short name for the outfit.
         * @example "Storm gear"
         */
        name: string;
        /**
         * What the outfit looks like, with colours and materials. An outfit with no description is not created.
         * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
         * @example "yellow sou'wester hat and full-length yellow oilskins over the jumper"
         */
        description?: string;
      }[];
      /**
       * A one- or two-sentence description of the whole look.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "A tall woman in her early 30s with tied-back black hair, a silver streak and wire glasses, in a navy oilskin coat."
       */
      summary?: string;
    };
  }[];
  /**
   * How characters relate to each other, one entry per pair and direction.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   */
  relationships?: {
    /**
     * The key of the character the relationship is seen from. Must match a character key.
     * @example "ines"
     */
    from: string;
    /**
     * The key of the other character. Must match a character key.
     * @example "tomas"
     */
    to: string;
    /**
     * What the relationship is, in a word or two.
     * @example "reluctant respect"
     */
    kind: string;
    /**
     * Anything more about the relationship.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "She was sent to retire him; by the end she wants his advice."
     */
    notes?: string;
  }[];
  /**
   * The places the story uses. Each becomes a location in the project, unless one with the same key or name already exists.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   */
  locations?: {
    /**
     * A short lowercase slug for the place. Other fields refer to it by this key.
     * At least 1 characters.
     * @example "vell"
     */
    key: string;
    /**
     * The place's name as it appears in the project.
     * At least 1 characters.
     * @example "Vell Light"
     */
    name: string;
    /**
     * How the place looks. It becomes the location's first description version.
     */
    description: {
      /**
       * What sort of place it is: a room, building, street, vehicle interior, landscape and so on.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "building"
       */
      kind?: string;
      /**
       * Building style, construction and materials.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "whitewashed stone tower with an iron lantern room"
       */
      architecture?: string;
      /**
       * How the space is arranged, so it can be drawn the same way from any angle.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "spiral stair up the tower; keeper's cottage attached at the base, facing the harbour"
       */
      layout?: string;
      /**
       * The colours the place is built from.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "white stone, rust red ironwork, slate grey sea"
       */
      palette?: string;
      /**
       * The place's typical light. A panel falls back on it when neither its prompt draft nor its spec names lighting.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "cold overcast daylight; warm lamp glow from the lantern room at night"
       */
      lighting?: string;
      /**
       * The feeling the place gives.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "windswept and isolated, but cared for"
       */
      atmosphere?: string;
      /**
       * 3-6 features that make the place recognisable; panel images are asked to show them.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example ["red iron lantern gallery","brass lens behind the glass","seaweed-covered rocks at the base"]
       */
      keyFeatures?: string[];
      /**
       * Things about the place that must never change between images, one per item.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example ["tower is white with a red lantern room","cottage door faces the harbour"]
       */
      immutableTraits?: string[];
      /**
       * A one- or two-sentence description of the place. Panel image prompts use it to describe the location.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "A whitewashed stone lighthouse with a red iron lantern room on a rocky point, a small cottage at its foot."
       */
      summary?: string;
    };
  }[];
  /**
   * Important objects in the story.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   */
  props?: {
    /**
     * A short lowercase slug for the object. Other fields refer to it by this key.
     * At least 1 characters.
     * @example "notebook"
     */
    key: string;
    /**
     * The object's name as it appears in the project.
     * At least 1 characters.
     * @example "Ines's weather notebook"
     */
    name: string;
    /**
     * Whether the object matters visually across several scenes. Only recurring props are added to the project.
     * Optional — defaults to false when left out.
     * @example true
     */
    recurring?: boolean;
    /**
     * How the object looks. It becomes the prop's first description version.
     */
    description: {
      /**
       * What sort of object it is.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "pocket notebook"
       */
      kind?: string;
      /**
       * What it is made of.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "oilcloth cover, lined paper"
       */
      material?: string;
      /**
       * How big it is.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "palm-sized"
       */
      size?: string;
      /**
       * Its colours.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "dark green cover, cream pages, red elastic band"
       */
      colors?: string;
      /**
       * Details that make the object recognisable, one per item.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example ["red elastic band","dog-eared corners"]
       */
      keyFeatures?: string[];
      /**
       * Things about the object that must never change between images. Panel prompts list them next to the prop.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example ["dark green cover","red elastic band"]
       */
      immutableTraits?: string[];
      /**
       * A one- or two-sentence description of the object. Panel image prompts use it to describe the prop.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "A palm-sized notebook with a dark green oilcloth cover held shut by a red elastic band."
       */
      summary?: string;
    };
  }[];
  /**
   * Facts about the story's world that hold everywhere in it.
   * Optional — defaults to {"worldRules":[],"factions":[],"uniforms":[],"technology":"","magicSystem":"","recurringScenery":[],"vehicles":[],"notes":""} when left out.
   */
  world?: {
    /**
     * Rules of the world, one per item. Added to the project's world notes.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["the lamp must be lit from sunset to sunrise","the supply boat comes once a fortnight"]
     */
    worldRules?: string[];
    /**
     * Groups, organisations or sides in the story. Added to the project's world notes.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     */
    factions?: {
      /**
       * The group's name.
       * @example "Coastal Lights Board"
       */
      name: string;
      /**
       * Who they are and what they want.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "The authority replacing keepers with automatic lamps."
       */
      description?: string;
    }[];
    /**
     * Uniforms worn in the story, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["Lights Board navy coat with brass buttons"]
     */
    uniforms?: string[];
    /**
     * The level and kind of technology. Added to the project's world notes.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "paraffin lamps, clockwork lens drive, radio telephone"
     */
    technology?: string;
    /**
     * How magic works, if there is any; added to the world notes. When there is none, leave it empty or say so.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "none; the lamp turning by itself is never explained"
     */
    magicSystem?: string;
    /**
     * Backgrounds that come back often, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["the harbour wall","the spiral stair"]
     */
    recurringScenery?: string[];
    /**
     * Vehicles in the story, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["the fortnightly supply boat"]
     */
    vehicles?: string[];
    /**
     * Anything else about the world.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "The village of Vell is across the bay and never shown up close."
     */
    notes?: string;
  };
  /**
   * The story's major events, in order. Shown for review with the analysis.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   */
  plotBeats?: {
    /**
     * The beat's position in the story, counting from 1.
     * Between -9007199254740991 and 9007199254740991.
     * @example 1
     */
    order: number;
    /**
     * What happens in this beat.
     * @example "Ines arrives at Vell with orders to shut down the light."
     */
    summary: string;
    /**
     * Keys of the characters in this beat. Each must match a character key.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["ines","tomas"]
     */
    characters?: string[];
    /**
     * The key of the place the beat happens in. Must match a location key.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "vell"
     */
    locationKey?: string;
  }[];
  /**
   * The story split into chapters at natural breaks; at least one. Each becomes a chapter in the project, with its part of the source text attached.
   * At least 1 items.
   */
  chapters: {
    /**
     * The chapter's position, counting from 1.
     * Between -9007199254740991 and 9007199254740991.
     * @example 1
     */
    order: number;
    /**
     * The chapter's title. A chapter whose title already exists from an earlier analysis is skipped.
     * @example "The Last Keeper"
     */
    title: string;
    /**
     * What happens in the chapter and what has changed by its end.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Ines reaches Vell and meets Tomas, who refuses to leave; she agrees to stay until the storm passes."
     */
    summary?: string;
    /**
     * The first ~12 words of the chapter, copied exactly from the source text. The app searches for them to cut the source into chapters; if they cannot be found, the text is split evenly instead.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "The supply boat left Ines on the jetty at Vell just as the wind"
     */
    sourceStart?: string;
    /**
     * The chapter's main beats, in order, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["Ines lands at Vell","Tomas refuses to leave","the storm comes in"]
     */
    beats?: string[];
  }[];
}
```

## StoryRewrite

Asked by **Rewrite story** — returns a rewritten story following your instruction.

```ts
/** A rewritten version of the story, following the editor's instruction. */
interface StoryRewrite {
  /**
   * The full rewritten story text. It is saved as a new revision of the story.
   * At least 1 characters.
   * @example "The supply boat left Ines on the jetty at Vell just as the wind turned. Up on the point, the lamp was already lit."
   */
  content: string;
  /**
   * A short note on what was changed. Returned with the result; not part of the story.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "Tightened the opening and moved the storm warning earlier."
   */
  notes?: string;
}
```

<details><summary>Complete example</summary>

```json
{
  "content": "The supply boat left Ines on the jetty at Vell just as the wind turned. Up on the point, the lamp was already lit.",
  "notes": "Tightened the opening and moved the storm warning earlier."
}
```

</details>

## ChapterOutline

Asked by **Plan chapter**, first question — the chapter's scenes, before any pages.

```ts
/** One chapter broken into scenes, without pages yet; each scene's pages are planned in a later step. */
interface ChapterOutline {
  /**
   * What happens in the chapter. Replaces the chapter's summary when not empty.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "Ines reaches Vell and meets Tomas, who refuses to leave; she agrees to stay until the storm passes."
   */
  chapterSummary?: string;
  /**
   * How things stand when the chapter opens.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "Ines is on her way to close the light; Tomas is alone at Vell."
   */
  openingState?: string;
  /**
   * How things stand when the chapter ends. The next chapter's planning receives it.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "Ines and Tomas are shut in the tower together as the storm starts."
   */
  closingState?: string;
  /**
   * How characters have changed by the end of the chapter, one per item. The next chapter's planning receives them.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   * @example ["Ines: coat soaked through","Tomas: has read the closure order"]
   */
  characterStateChanges?: string[];
  /**
   * How places have changed by the end of the chapter, one per item.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   * @example ["Vell Light: storm shutters closed"]
   */
  locationStateChanges?: string[];
  /**
   * Facts the reader learns in this chapter, one per item. The next chapter's planning receives them.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   * @example ["Tomas has kept the light for forty years"]
   */
  revealedFacts?: string[];
  /**
   * The chapter's scenes in story order; at least one. Each becomes a scene of the chapter.
   * At least 1 items.
   */
  scenes: {
    /**
     * A short title for the scene. The page-planning step names the scene it plans by this title.
     * @example "Arrival at Vell"
     */
    title: string;
    /**
     * What happens in the scene.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Ines climbs from the jetty to the lighthouse and meets Tomas at the door."
     */
    summary?: string;
    /**
     * The key of the place the scene happens in. Must match a location key from the prompt's project data.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "vell"
     */
    locationKey?: string;
    /**
     * Time of day.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "late afternoon"
     */
    time?: string;
    /**
     * The weather in the scene.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "rising wind, low grey cloud"
     */
    weather?: string;
    /**
     * Keys of the characters present. Each must match a character key from the prompt's project data.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["ines","tomas"]
     */
    characterKeys?: string[];
    /**
     * What the scene does for the story.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "set up the conflict between Ines and Tomas"
     */
    purpose?: string;
    /**
     * How the scene opens.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Ines alone on the jetty as the boat leaves"
     */
    opening?: string;
    /**
     * How the scene develops.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "she climbs to the tower; Tomas opens the door but blocks it"
     */
    progression?: string;
    /**
     * The scene's high point.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Tomas tears up the closure order"
     */
    climax?: string;
    /**
     * How the scene ends.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "he steps aside to let her in out of the rain"
     */
    ending?: string;
    /**
     * Things that must stay consistent through the scene, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["Ines carries her notebook in her coat pocket"]
     */
    continuityNotes?: string[];
    /**
     * Continuity facts at the start of the scene, keyed by who or what they are about.
     * Optional — defaults to {} when left out.
     * @example {"ines":"dry, coat buttoned","tomas":"in shirtsleeves"}
     */
    initialState?: Record<string, string>;
    /**
     * Continuity facts at the end of the scene, keyed by who or what they are about.
     * Optional — defaults to {} when left out.
     * @example {"ines":"soaked through","tomas":"holding the torn order"}
     */
    finalState?: Record<string, string>;
    /**
     * What changed during the scene, one per item, written as "who: what changed".
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["Ines: coat soaked through"]
     */
    continuityDeltas?: string[];
    /**
     * The scene's beats in order, one per item. Each is saved as a story beat of the scene.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["the boat leaves","Tomas blocks the door","the order is torn up"]
     */
    beats?: string[];
  }[];
}
```

```json
{
  "chapterSummary": "Ines reaches Vell and meets Tomas, who refuses to leave; she agrees to stay until the storm passes.",
  "openingState": "Ines is on her way to close the light; Tomas is alone at Vell.",
  "closingState": "Ines and Tomas are shut in the tower together as the storm starts.",
  "characterStateChanges": [
    "Ines: coat soaked through",
    "Tomas: has read the closure order"
  ],
  "locationStateChanges": [
    "Vell Light: storm shutters closed"
  ],
  "revealedFacts": [
    "Tomas has kept the light for forty years"
  ],
  "scenes": [
    {
      "title": "Arrival at Vell",
      "summary": "Ines climbs from the jetty to the lighthouse and meets Tomas at the door.",
      "locationKey": "vell",
      "time": "late afternoon",
      "weather": "rising wind, low grey cloud",
      "characterKeys": [
        "ines",
        "tomas"
      ],

      "progression": "she climbs to the tower; Tomas opens the door but blocks it",
      "climax": "Tomas tears up the closure order",
      "ending": "he steps aside to let her in out of the rain",
      "continuityNotes": [
        "Ines carries her notebook in her coat pocket"
      ],

        "ines": "dry, coat buttoned",
        "tomas": "in shirtsleeves"
      },

        "ines": "soaked through",
        "tomas": "holding the torn order"
      },
      "continuityDeltas": [
        "Ines: coat soaked through"
      ],
      "beats": [
        "the boat leaves",
        "Tomas blocks the door",
        "the order is torn up"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## ScenePages

Asked by **Plan chapter**, one question per scene — that scene's pages and panels. For a film project these are shots, for a vertical strip one panel per page with height and seam.

```ts
/** The pages of one scene, each with its panels, panel specs and lettering. */
interface ScenePages {
  /**
   * The scene's pages in reading order; at least one.
   * At least 1 items.
   */
  pages: {
    /**
     * What the page does for the story.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "introduce Vell Light and Ines's arrival"
     */
    purpose?: string;
    /**
     * How fast the page reads.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "slow, lingering"
     */
    pacing?: string;
    /**
     * What the page should make the reader look at.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "the lighthouse against the sky"
     */
    visualEmphasis?: string;
    /**
     * What pulls the reader on to the next page.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "a figure watching from the lantern room"
     */
    pageTurnHook?: string;
    /**
     * One of the layout template keys the prompt lists, with the same number of panels as this page. If it does not fit, a default layout for that panel count is used. Film and vertical projects always use "full-page".
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "full-page"
     */
    layoutTemplate?: string;
    /**
     * The page's panels in reading order, 1 to 5.
     * Between 1 and 5 items.
     */
    panels: {
      /**
       * What the panel shows. It is saved as the panel's spec and drives its image prompt.
       */
      spec: {
        /**
         * The single moment the panel shows, as one visible action. Stored as the panel's story beat.
         * @example "Ines looks up at the lighthouse from the end of the jetty."
         */
        beat: string;
        /**
         * How much of the scene the frame takes in, from very wide to a detail.
         * Optional — defaults to "medium" when left out.
         * @example "wide"
         */
        shotType: "extreme-wide" | "wide" | "full" | "medium" | "medium-close" | "close" | "extreme-close" | "insert";
        /**
         * Where the camera looks from.
         * Optional — defaults to "eye-level" when left out.
         * @example "low"
         */
        cameraAngle: "eye-level" | "low" | "high" | "birds-eye" | "worms-eye" | "over-shoulder" | "dutch" | "pov";
        /**
         * Exactly the characters visible in the panel. Characters that cannot be matched to the cast are dropped.
         * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
         */
        characters?: {
          /**
           * The character's key (or id) from the prompt's project data.
           * @example "ines"
           */
          characterId: string;
          /**
           * The character's facial expression.
           * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
           * @example "wary, squinting into the wind"
           */
          expression?: string;
          /**
           * The character's pose.
           * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
           * @example "standing, one hand holding her hat"
           */
          pose?: string;
          /**
           * What the character is doing.
           * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
           * @example "looking up at the tower"
           */
          action?: string;
          /**
           * The outfit, only if it changes. Naming one of the character's outfits (project data lists them under outfits) switches the character into it from this panel on, reference image included, until another is named; anything else describes this panel's wardrobe.
           * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
           * @example "Storm gear, hood up"
           */
          outfit?: string;
          /**
           * Where the character is in the frame. Also used to point the speech bubble's tail at the speaker.
           * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
           * @example "left foreground"
           */
          position?: string;
        }[];
        /**
         * The key (or id) of the panel's location from the prompt's project data. Leave it out to use the scene's location.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         * @example "vell"
         */
        locationId?: string;
        /**
         * The focal subject and where it sits in the frame.
         * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
         * @example "Ines small in the lower left, the tower filling the right two thirds"
         */
        composition?: string;
        /**
         * What is in the foreground; best drawn from the location's key features.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         * @example "wet planks of the jetty"
         */
        foreground?: string;
        /**
         * What is in the middle distance.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         * @example "seaweed-covered rocks at the base"
         */
        midground?: string;
        /**
         * What is in the background.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         * @example "the white tower and red lantern room against low cloud"
         */
        background?: string;
        /**
         * Light source, direction and colour temperature. Must stay inside the project's art direction.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         * @example "cold overcast daylight from the left"
         */
        lighting?: string;
        /**
         * The feeling of the panel; the image prompt adds it as the mood. Must stay inside the project's art direction.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         * @example "quiet unease"
         */
        emotion?: string;
        /**
         * The panel's main action. Used when the panel has no prompt draft action.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         * @example "Ines stops and looks up at the tower"
         */
        action?: string;
        /**
         * Facts that must visibly carry over from earlier panels, one per item. Added to the image prompt.
         * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
         * @example ["notebook in her coat pocket"]
         */
        continuityRequirements?: string[];
        /**
         * Where to keep the image calm so lettering can be added later. Plan it for every panel with dialogue or narration; leave it out for film projects.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         */
        negativeSpace?: {
          /**
           * The part of the frame to keep clear.
           * @example "upper left sky"
           */
          area: string;
          /**
           * What will go in that space.
           * @example "dialogue"
           */
          purpose: "dialogue" | "narration" | "sfx";
        };
        /**
         * Keys (or ids) of props from the prompt's project data that appear in the panel. Unknown keys are dropped.
         * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
         * @example ["notebook"]
         */
        propIds?: string[];
        /**
         * Leave empty. The app fills it with the ids of the bubbles it creates from `dialogue`.
         * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
         * @example []
         */
        dialogueIds?: string[];
        /**
         * Leave empty. The app fills it with the ids of the captions it creates from `narration`.
         * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
         * @example []
         */
        narrationIds?: string[];
        /**
         * Leave empty. The app fills it with the ids of the sound effects it creates from `sfx`.
         * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
         * @example []
         */
        sfxIds?: string[];
        /**
         * Vertical strips only: how long the reader spends on the panel, which sets its height in the strip. "short" reads fast, "tall" and "very-tall" hold a moment. Ignored by other formats.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         * @example "tall"
         */
        height?: "short" | "normal" | "tall" | "very-tall";
        /**
         * Vertical strips only: how this panel meets the one above it. The first panel of a chapter needs none. Ignored by other formats.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         */
        seam?: {
          /**
           * "gap" shows background between panels (a beat change); "butt" joins them with no break (action continues); "bleed" overlaps with a hard edge; "dissolve" overlaps with a blend; "fade" fades both edges into a colour (a change of scene, place or time).
           * Optional — defaults to "gap" when left out.
           * @example "fade"
           */
          kind?: "gap" | "butt" | "bleed" | "dissolve" | "fade";
          /**
           * Pixels at the strip's width: the gap, the overlap depth, or the fade band. Leave it out to size it from the panels it joins.
           * Between 0 and 2000.
           * Optional — may be left out.
           * @example 120
           */
          size?: number;
          /**
           * The colour to fade through, as a hex code; only used by "fade". Defaults to the strip background.
           * Must match /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/.
           * Optional — may be left out.
           * @example "#0b0f1a"
           */
          color?: string;
        };
      };
      /**
       * Speech bubbles in the panel, in reading order; each at most about 20 words. Leave empty for film projects.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       */
      dialogue?: {
        /**
         * The speaker's character key, or empty when the speaker is off-panel. The bubble's tail points at them.
         * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
         * @example "tomas"
         */
        speaker?: string;
        /**
         * The words in the bubble.
         * @example "You're the one they sent to put out my light."
         */
        text: string;
        /**
         * The bubble style: spoken, thought, shouted or whispered.
         * Optional — defaults to "normal" when left out.
         * @example "shout"
         */
        kind: "normal" | "thought" | "shout" | "whisper";
        /**
         * Where in the panel the bubble should go if there is room. Leave it out to let the app choose.
         * Optional — may be left out.
         * @example "top-right"
         */
        preferredQuadrant?: "top-left" | "top-right" | "bottom-left" | "bottom-right" | "top" | "bottom";
      }[];
      /**
       * Caption text for the panel, one caption per item. Optional.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example ["The light at Vell had not gone dark in forty years."]
       */
      narration?: string[];
      /**
       * Sound effects drawn in the panel, one per item. Leave empty for film projects.
       * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
       * @example ["WHOOSH"]
       */
      sfx?: string[];
    }[];
  }[];
}
```

## PanelPromptDraft

Asked by **Prepare page prompts** — per-panel prompt text for the image model.

```ts
/** Image-prompt sections written for each panel of a page, from the panel's planned data. */
interface PanelPromptDraft {
  /**
   * One entry per panel of the page.
   */
  panels: {
    /**
     * The id of the panel this entry is for, copied from the panels in the prompt. Entries with an unknown id are ignored.
     * @example "3f2b8c1e-7a4d-4e0b-9c6a-1d5e8f2a7b90"
     */
    panelId: string;
    /**
     * The story moment in one sentence. Used as the panel's intent in the image prompt, in place of the beat.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Ines arrives and sees the lighthouse she has come to shut down."
     */
    intent?: string;
    /**
     * One visible physical action per character, at its clearest instant. Used in place of the spec's action.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Ines stands at the end of the jetty, head tipped back, one hand holding her hat on."
     */
    action?: string;
    /**
     * Face and body language that show the emotion.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "narrowed eyes, mouth set, shoulders hunched against the wind"
     */
    expression?: string;
    /**
     * The focal subject, where it sits in the frame, depth and what leads the eye. Used in place of the spec's composition.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Ines small in the lower left; the jetty leads the eye to the tower on the right"
     */
    composition?: string;
    /**
     * The light source, its direction and colour temperature. Used in place of the spec's lighting.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "cold overcast daylight from the left, soft shadows"
     */
    lighting?: string;
    /**
     * Only facts that must visibly carry over, one per item. Added to the image prompt's continuity list.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["coat buttoned and dry","notebook in her coat pocket"]
     */
    continuity?: string[];
  }[];
}
```

<details><summary>Complete example</summary>

```json
{
  "panels": [
    {
      "panelId": "3f2b8c1e-7a4d-4e0b-9c6a-1d5e8f2a7b90",
      "intent": "Ines arrives and sees the lighthouse she has come to shut down.",
      "action": "Ines stands at the end of the jetty, head tipped back, one hand holding her hat on.",
      "expression": "narrowed eyes, mouth set, shoulders hunched against the wind",
      "composition": "Ines small in the lower left; the jetty leads the eye to the tower on the right",
      "lighting": "cold overcast daylight from the left, soft shadows",
      "continuity": [
        "coat buttoned and dry",
        "notebook in her coat pocket"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

## NarrationDraft

Asked by **Generate narration** — the narrator's lines, tied to panels.

```ts
/** Voice-over narration for a chapter, each line tied to the panel it is read over. */
interface NarrationDraft {
  /**
   * The narration lines in reading order. At least 90% of the chapter's panels must have a line with their panelId, and the total word count must reach at least 70% of (number of panels x the words per panel the prompt asks for); otherwise the answer is sent back for repair.
   */
  lines: {
    /**
     * The spoken line: 1-3 sentences, in the target language, with no labels or markup.
     * At least 1 characters.
     * @example "The boat was already turning for home when Ines looked up and saw the light at Vell, burning in broad daylight."
     */
    text: string;
    /**
     * The id of the panel this line is read over. Must be one of the panel ids listed in the prompt.
     * At least 1 characters.
     * @example "panel-1"
     */
    panelId: string;
  }[];
}
```

<details><summary>Complete example</summary>

```json
{
  "lines": [
    {
      "text": "The boat was already turning for home when Ines looked up and saw the light at Vell, burning in broad daylight.",
      "panelId": "panel-1"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

## ImageDescription

Asked by **Describe image** — what a reference image shows, by the aspects you asked for. Attach the image.

```ts
/** A description of a reference image, covering only the aspects that were asked for. */
interface ImageDescription {
  /**
   * One or two sentences about the image as a whole. Always filled.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "A woman in a navy oilskin coat stands on a wet jetty, looking up at a white lighthouse under low cloud."
   */
  overview?: string;
  /**
   * How the image is drawn, not what it shows. It can be used as the project's art style; its fields then go into the art direction of every image prompt.
   * Optional — may be left out.
   */
  style?: {
    /**
     * The style in one or two sentences.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Clean ink linework with flat muted colour and soft cel shading."
     */
    summary?: string;
    /**
     * Line weight and quality.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "fine, even ink lines, heavier on outer contours"
     */
    lineTreatment?: string;
    /**
     * How colour is used.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "full colour, muted blues and greys with red accents"
     */
    colorPolicy?: string;
    /**
     * How shading is done.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "two-tone cel shading"
     */
    shading?: string;
    /**
     * How much detail there is.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "detailed backgrounds, simpler figures"
     */
    detailLevel?: string;
    /**
     * How faces are drawn.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "realistic proportions, small eyes, minimal nose line"
     */
    faceRendering?: string;
    /**
     * How backgrounds are drawn.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "painted skies, inked architecture"
     */
    backgroundRendering?: string;
    /**
     * How movement is shown.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "none; still, posed frames"
     */
    motionEffects?: string;
    /**
     * The contrast level.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "medium, soft"
     */
    contrast?: string;
    /**
     * Screen tones, if any. Dropped from prompts for colour projects.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "none"
     */
    screenTones?: string;
    /**
     * The lighting approach of the style.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "diffuse natural light, few hard shadows"
     */
    lighting?: string;
    /**
     * What the style clearly avoids, one per item. Image prompts list them under "Avoid".
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["photoreal rendering","heavy speed lines"]
     */
    exclusions?: string[];
  };
  /**
   * The most prominent figure, as a character bible. It can be used to create a character. Leave a field empty rather than inventing what the image does not show.
   * Optional — may be left out.
   */
  character?: {
    /**
     * How the character presents, as it should be drawn.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "woman"
     */
    genderPresentation?: string;
    /**
     * Apparent age, best as a number range.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "early 30s"
     */
    ageRange?: string;
    /**
     * Height, ideally relative to the rest of the cast.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "tall, a head above Tomas"
     */
    height?: string;
    /**
     * Body shape and frame.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "lean, long-limbed"
     */
    build?: string;
    /**
     * The shape of the face.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "narrow oval with a pointed chin"
     */
    faceShape?: string;
    /**
     * Skin tone. The image prompt adds the word "skin" after it.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "light olive"
     */
    skinTone?: string;
    /**
     * Eye shape and colour.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "hooded grey eyes"
     */
    eyes?: string;
    /**
     * Eyebrow shape and colour.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "straight dark brows"
     */
    eyebrows?: string;
    /**
     * Nose shape.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "long straight nose"
     */
    nose?: string;
    /**
     * Mouth and lips.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "thin lips, often pressed together"
     */
    mouth?: string;
    /**
     * Exact hair colour, length and style.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "shoulder-length black hair tied back, a silver streak at the left temple"
     */
    hair?: string;
    /**
     * Beard or moustache; leave empty when there is none.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example ""
     */
    facialHair?: string;
    /**
     * Visible marks that help tell the character apart, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["small faded mark on the right cheekbone","ink stains on the fingertips"]
     */
    distinctiveFeatures?: string[];
    /**
     * The default outfit with colours and materials. It becomes the character's "Default" outfit and is drawn whenever a panel names no other outfit.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "navy oilskin coat over a grey wool jumper, dark canvas trousers, black rubber boots"
     */
    wardrobe?: string;
    /**
     * Things the character wears besides clothes, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["round wire glasses","brass pocket watch"]
     */
    accessories?: string[];
    /**
     * Weapons the character carries, one per item; empty when none.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example []
     */
    weapons?: string[];
    /**
     * Objects the character usually carries, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["weather notebook","pencil stub"]
     */
    props?: string[];
    /**
     * Personality in a few words. Kept apart from appearance so it never reaches the drawing as a look.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "precise, stubborn, quietly kind"
     */
    personality?: string;
    /**
     * How the personality shows in posture and gesture; the image prompt uses it for the character's reference sheet.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "taps her pencil against the notebook when thinking"
     */
    visualMannerisms?: string;
    /**
     * The expression the character wears when a panel does not say otherwise.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "focused, slight frown"
     */
    defaultExpression?: string;
    /**
     * 3-6 short, visible identity markers that must stay the same in every panel. The image prompt lists them as "never change". Never put personality or plot facts here.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["silver streak in black hair","round wire glasses","navy oilskin coat"]
     */
    immutableTraits?: string[];
    /**
     * Other outfits the character wears in the story. Each one with a description becomes an extra outfit for the character, next to the default wardrobe.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     */
    outfitVariants?: {
      /**
       * A short name for the outfit.
       * @example "Storm gear"
       */
      name: string;
      /**
       * What the outfit looks like, with colours and materials. An outfit with no description is not created.
       * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
       * @example "yellow sou'wester hat and full-length yellow oilskins over the jumper"
       */
      description?: string;
    }[];
    /**
     * A one- or two-sentence description of the whole look.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "A tall woman in her early 30s with tied-back black hair, a silver streak and wire glasses, in a navy oilskin coat."
     */
    summary?: string;
  };
  /**
   * The clothing in its own right, in enough detail to redraw it on another figure.
   * Optional — may be left out.
   */
  outfit?: {
    /**
     * Outfit in one or two sentences.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "A long navy oilskin coat over a grey jumper, with dark trousers and black boots."
     */
    summary?: string;
    /**
     * Specific points about the outfit, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["coat buttoned to the collar","wool jumper with a ribbed neck","boots wet to the ankle"]
     */
    details?: string[];
  };
  /**
   * The setting behind and around the subject. It can be used to create a location.
   * Optional — may be left out.
   */
  location?: {
    /**
     * What sort of place it is: a room, building, street, vehicle interior, landscape and so on.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "building"
     */
    kind?: string;
    /**
     * Building style, construction and materials.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "whitewashed stone tower with an iron lantern room"
     */
    architecture?: string;
    /**
     * How the space is arranged, so it can be drawn the same way from any angle.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "spiral stair up the tower; keeper's cottage attached at the base, facing the harbour"
     */
    layout?: string;
    /**
     * The colours the place is built from.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "white stone, rust red ironwork, slate grey sea"
     */
    palette?: string;
    /**
     * The place's typical light. A panel falls back on it when neither its prompt draft nor its spec names lighting.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "cold overcast daylight; warm lamp glow from the lantern room at night"
     */
    lighting?: string;
    /**
     * The feeling the place gives.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "windswept and isolated, but cared for"
     */
    atmosphere?: string;
    /**
     * 3-6 features that make the place recognisable; panel images are asked to show them.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["red iron lantern gallery","brass lens behind the glass","seaweed-covered rocks at the base"]
     */
    keyFeatures?: string[];
    /**
     * Things about the place that must never change between images, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["tower is white with a red lantern room","cottage door faces the harbour"]
     */
    immutableTraits?: string[];
    /**
     * A one- or two-sentence description of the place. Panel image prompts use it to describe the location.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "A whitewashed stone lighthouse with a red iron lantern room on a rocky point, a small cottage at its foot."
     */
    summary?: string;
  };
  /**
   * Key light, shadows, time of day and the palette the image is built from.
   * Optional — may be left out.
   */
  lighting?: {
    /**
     * Lighting in one or two sentences.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Flat overcast daylight from the left, cool and low in contrast."
     */
    summary?: string;
    /**
     * Specific points about the lighting, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["no hard shadows","dominant slate grey, accent red"]
     */
    details?: string[];
  };
  /**
   * Shot type, camera angle, how the frame is divided and where the eye goes.
   * Optional — may be left out.
   */
  composition?: {
    /**
     * Composition in one or two sentences.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Low-angle wide shot; the figure small in the lower left, the tower filling the right."
     */
    summary?: string;
    /**
     * Specific points about the composition, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["jetty leads the eye to the tower","horizon in the lower third"]
     */
    details?: string[];
  };
  /**
   * The feeling the image carries and the choices that create it.
   * Optional — may be left out.
   */
  mood?: {
    /**
     * Mood in one or two sentences.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Lonely and uneasy, softened by the warm lamp."
     */
    summary?: string;
    /**
     * Specific points about the mood, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["small figure against a large tower","cold palette with one warm light"]
     */
    details?: string[];
  };
  /**
   * Notable objects, weapons, furniture and set dressing.
   * Optional — may be left out.
   */
  props?: {
    /**
     * Props in one or two sentences.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "A small green notebook sticks out of the coat pocket."
     */
    summary?: string;
    /**
     * Specific points about the props, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["notebook with a red elastic band","coil of rope on the jetty"]
     */
    details?: string[];
  };
  /**
   * The period and cultural setting the image suggests, and the cues that place it.
   * Optional — may be left out.
   */
  era?: {
    /**
     * Era in one or two sentences.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Mid-20th-century northern European coast."
     */
    summary?: string;
    /**
     * Specific points about the era, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["oilskin workwear","paraffin lamp in the lantern room"]
     */
    details?: string[];
  };
  /**
   * The apparent medium and process.
   * Optional — may be left out.
   */
  technique?: {
    /**
     * Technique in one or two sentences.
     * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
     * @example "Digital ink with flat colour and a light paper grain."
     */
    summary?: string;
    /**
     * Specific points about the technique, one per item.
     * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
     * @example ["visible paper texture","no halftone"]
     */
    details?: string[];
  };
  /**
   * The answer to the caller's own question, when the prompt includes one; otherwise empty.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example ""
   */
  custom?: string;
  /**
   * What could not be told from the image, one per item. Better than a confident guess.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   * @example ["eye colour (face in shadow)"]
   */
  uncertain?: string[];
}
```

## PanelCheck

Asked by **Check panel** — a consistency check of finished artwork against its cast. Attach the image.

```ts
/** A check of one generated panel image against the characters it was supposed to show. */
interface PanelCheck {
  /**
   * How many distinct people or human-like figures are visible, including background and partial figures. A count different from the expected cast marks the panel as a mismatch.
   * Between 0 and 100.
   * @example 2
   */
  peopleCount: number;
  /**
   * Names of the expected characters (as listed in the prompt) that are clearly in the image.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   * @example ["Ines","Tomas"]
   */
  expectedCharactersPresent?: string[];
  /**
   * Names of the expected characters that are not in the image. Any entry marks the panel as a mismatch.
   * Optional — defaults to [] when left out.
   * @example []
   */
  missingCharacters?: string[];
  /**
   * How many visible people are not one of the expected characters. More than zero marks the panel as a mismatch.
   * Between 0 and 100.
   * Optional — defaults to 0 when left out.
   * @example 0
   */
  unexpectedPeople?: number;
  /**
   * true only when the image contains legible letters or words (signs, speech bubbles, captions, screens). Saved with the check.
   * Optional — defaults to false when left out.
   * @example false
   */
  readableText?: boolean;
  /**
   * Anything else worth noting. Saved with the check.
   * Optional — defaults to "" when left out.
   * @example "Tomas is partly hidden behind the door."
   */
  notes?: string;
}
```

<details><summary>Complete example</summary>

```json
{
  "peopleCount": 2,
  "expectedCharactersPresent": [
    "Ines",
    "Tomas"
  ],
  "missingCharacters": [],
  "unexpectedPeople": 0,
  "readableText": false,
  "notes": "Tomas is partly hidden behind the door."
}
```

</details>
